gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns the invalid promotion of local implicit-function uniqueness to a global singleton state set and the resulting identification of the globally infimized cost with one branch. ISSUE-001 instead diagnoses an invalid finite-element gradient/error estimate; it does not recognize the global-versus-local solution-set or infimum-attainment defect.

The gold issue is a missing proof-required L^p hypothesis for the desired state in an adjoint maximum-norm and second-variation estimate, together with malformed dimension notation. ISSUE-001 addresses a separate invalid inverse-estimate argument for a state discretization gradient error and does not identify the missing regularity assumption.

The gold issue concerns the failure to define a discrete reduced objective when arbitrary controls may have multiple discrete states, and the absence of a selected local branch. ISSUE-001 concerns only a false gradient approximation estimate and does not recognize the well-definedness or branch-selection obligation for J_h.

The gold issue is the unsupported quantification over an arbitrary semidiscrete solution when convergence is known only for a specifically constructed sequence of local minimizers. ISSUE-001 instead rejects a spatial gradient-rate inference; it does not identify the missing sequence-selection and convergence premise.

Both identify the same failed approximation step: the proof incorrectly derives an O(h^2) gradient/discrete error estimate from an O(h^2) L2 state error using inverse estimates, despite the continuous component and only H2 regularity. The prediction also supplies the integration-by-parts repair that avoids differentiating the error and restores the required adjoint estimate.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof cannot obtain the required O(h^2) gradient or auxiliary-adjoint bound by applying an inverse estimate to the full continuous-minus-discrete state error; the continuous interpolation remainder prevents that inference. The valid repair transfers derivatives by integration by parts and closes the estimate using the L2 state error and adjoint bounds.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed O(h^2) gradient estimate from an O(h^2) L2 state error is invalid because inverse estimates apply only to discrete functions and the continuous error component has insufficient approximation order; this leaves the auxiliary-adjoint and control-rate estimate unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly identifies both the invalid applicability and lost-order problem, states the resulting rate consequence, and gives the specific integration-by-parts repair based on L2, W^{1,4}, and L-infinity bounds.
